DL11.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,
How are you? I'm writing from way up north on the Klondike River.
I'm in Canada, just a few miles shy of the border with Alaska.

They've found gold in these parts, and I aim to find some myself.
Since your family was always good to me, I thought I would let 
you in on the loot.
If you lend me $75, I can set up camp here and start gold hunting.
I promise to give you ten percent of all the gold I find.

What do you say, cousin? Will you take a chance?

Your cousin,

AL14.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.

I'm sorry I never heard back from you last year. I managed to                                                                                 scrape together the money I needed from other friends and                                                                                         relatives. I worked day and night on the Klondike River, and                                                                                     found $2,000 worth of gold. All's well that ends well, as they say.

Please give my regards to the family. Tell them I'm on my way to                                                                            New York.   I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe                                                                                    I can do business with them.

Your cousin George

AL15.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.  I was sorry                                                                                I never heard back from you last year. I managed to scrape together                                                              the money I needed from other friends and relatives. I worked day                                                                     and night on the Klondike River, but I didn't find any gold. At least I                                                                     didn't starve or freeze to death. All's well that ends well, as they say.

Please give my regards to the family.  Tell them I'm on my way to                                                                       New York. I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe I can                                                                    do business with them.

Your cousin George

DL28.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

It's been a long time since we've been in touch. I've been                                                                                         working my way east from the West Coast, buying and 
selling properties on the way. Now I'm nearby, in the town                                                                                              of  Wichita, Kansas. Not far from here, some folks have                                                                                               struck oil.  I'm buying up land in the neighborhood so that                                                                                              I can strike it rich too! I thought I'd give you the first shot at                                                                                        investing in the well we're digging.  It will only cost you $800.                                                                                       You will get  20 percent of our profit.  If we strike oil, we could                                                                                      make millions!  Are you willing to take a chance?

Yours Cousin George.

AL29.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I have good news for you. We've struck oil! 
We've been pumping for about six months now, and the well is
finally dry. Your share of the profit is $2,500.00. I have sent it directly
to your bank.

Thank you for your help, partner!

Yours,

AL30.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I'm afraid I don't have good news. It seems
that we picked a piece of land without any oil underneath it.

I'm sorry about the money you lost. I'm sure you'll make it up soon, 
selling wheat and corn.

Thank you for your help anyway.

Yours,

AL31.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I finally have a chance to write and tell you
my good news. We've struck oil! We've been pumping for about six 
months now, and the well is finally dry. My partners and I made a profit
of $12,500 from this well.

I hope next time we can work together.

Yours,

AL32.text:
Dear FIRSTNAME,

After a year of hard work, I'm afraid I don't have good news. 
It seems that I picked a piece of land without any oil underneath it.

It's just as well you didn't invest in this well. If I hear of a better deal,
I'll be sure to let you know.


Yours,

DL19.text:
Dear Cousin, 

I hope you are doing well on your homestead on the range.

We are still living in New York City and working at the same jobs.

We have another chance to start a business with some friends. 
Once again, are you interested in investing $500.00
in our business?
If you invest, you'll get five percent of the profits.

I hope that you will write me soon.

Yours,

AL62.text:
Dear Cousin,

I have some bad news for you. Our biscuit company has gone 
out of business. We have lost a lot of money in the 
past three years, and we owe too much money to continue.
I have sent a final check to your bank. 

We will be fine. My sons and I have found work in factories 
in the city. When we save up enough money, we will try to 
start another business.

Thank you so much for your help in the past.
Fondly,

AL41.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Victory is very close. Last spring, Congress passed the
19th Amendment. Now we must wait and see how many 
states vote for it. It looks hopeful. I am having the time 
of my life working at NAWSA for a cause in which I believe.

I have other good news. A lawyer named Frederick Fields has 
helped me a lot in my work. We have become quite good friends 
during the past year. He has asked me to marry him, and I have                                                                  accepted. He is from Colorado, so we will surely come back                                                                                 west for the wedding.

Your loving daughter,

AL53.text:
Dear Ma and Pa,

Bob returned safely from France and sends his love. 
Bobby Jr., Mary, and little Harry are well.

Last spring, Congress passed the 19th Amendment,
which would give women the vote. For the past six months,
I've been doing volunteer work a few hours a week with the 
National American Woman Suffrage Association (NAWSA). 
We're trying to convince people to vote for this amendment.
It looks as though the amendment will be ratified. I'm so excited!

Your daughter,

YesHouse.text:
Congratulations! You have another son! Your monthly cost of living will increase by five dollars per month. 

My baby's name is:

Goal01.text: CONGRATULATIONS! You were a homestead farmer for 40 years. You did not reach the goal you set at the beginning, but you ran a profitable farm. Any pioneer would have been proud of your achievement.

NoHouse.text: Can you hear those folks in town talking? They'd like to meet you. Why don't you come by and say hello?

NoFence3.text: A few cattle broke down your wooden fence. They destroyed some of your crops. If you go to the general store and look at the catalog, I think you'll find exactly what you need.

FDB18.text: You were lucky. The summer rains started late this year. Your horse recovered and you finished plowing before the rain started.

FDBK19.text: You were lucky this time. The horses recovered and you finished plowing before the snow started.

Tractor.text: There aren't enough tractors for all of us. Make sure that you have a tractor for each worker you hire.

NoPlow6.text: I'm waiting for you to sell me your crops. I'll give you a good price.

GoBank.text: Go to the bank to collect your money.

BANK09.Tel.text:
TELEGRAM 
FROM: O'Grady Town
TO: Alla Ladizinsky

I have some bad news for you. On my way to O'Grady, 
I was caught in a sudden rainstorm. Part of your crop was ruined. I could only sell some of it. You can get your money from the cashier at the bank. I hope next time we'll have better luck.

CATALG10.text:
Ready-Made Wooden Fence
Build your own wooden fence to keep away intruders. The kit includes precut wooden pickets, posts, nails, and instructions. For only $200, you can buy enough wooden fencing to enclose a 160-acre farm. "Stake your claim!"

AL13.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.

Thank you for trusting me with your $75 last year. I worked day and night on the Klondike River, and found $2,000 worth of gold. A promise is a promise, so ten percent is yours. I have enclosed $200.

Please give my regards to the family. Tell them I'm on my way to New York. I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe I can do business with them.

Your cousin George
AL13.role: letter: Klondike loan repaid (Yes, gold found)

AL12.text:
Dear [FIRSTNAME],

I'm writing this letter while I ride the rails back east.

Thank you for trusting me with your $75 last year. I worked day and night on the Klondike River, but I didn't find any gold. I'm sorry that I lost your money. At least I didn't starve or freeze to death. All's well that ends well, as they say.

Please give my regards to the family. Tell them I'm on my way to New York. I want to get in touch with our relatives there. Maybe I can do business with them.

Your cousin George

DC_Retire.text: <Son1> takes over the homestead, and you hang up your plow. The neighbors come by to wish you well, and the whole town turns out to sing. Any pioneer would have been proud of your achievement.

DC_RetireInTown.text: <Son1> takes over the homestead, and you move into a house on Main Street in Longview. On warm evenings you sit outside the general store and listen to the town talk. Any pioneer would have been proud of your achievement.

DC_Kate1.text: Hello, neighbor! Billy and I are getting married this Saturday, and your whole family is invited. I sewed my dress myself on my new machine. After the wedding we're off to the fair in Chicago, and then to Kansas City. I'll miss Longview!

basis: TTALK talk 111 (married next month; the Exposition; Kansas City)

DC_Jesse1.text: Well, neighbor, this is goodbye. My train for California leaves at the end of the month. There's nothing for me to do here, and I'm not cut out for college, but I have to see the ocean for myself. Say goodbye to everyone in Longview for me. I'll see you around someday.
